sectionBreakdown.note: Take the Ross Lake water taxi to the Little Beaver dock, then start up the brush-choked Access/Perry Creek drainage toward the base of Southeast Mox. Devil's club and slide alder s…
sectionBreakdown.fromTo: Boat taxi + bushwhack into the approach drainage

sectionBreakdown.note: A second full day of brutal bushwhacking is needed just to reach the base of the 2,500-ft East Face — the FA party spent two full days on approach alone before touching rock.
sectionBreakdown.fromTo: Reach the base of the East Face

sectionBreakdown.note: About 1,000 ft of steep slabs lead to a small bivy ledge at the base of the near-vertical, 1,500-ft upper headwall. This sets up an early start on the crux the next day.
sectionBreakdown.fromTo: Climb the lower slabs to a bivy ledge

sectionBreakdown.note: An 18-hour push forces a route through steep, loose, poorly-protected 5.9+ A2- rock to the summit. The descent is a dozen-plus rappels off natural gear anchors (the route has no fi…
sectionBreakdown.fromTo: Summit push and all-night rappel descent

sectionBreakdown.note: After an all-night push, most parties take a slower recovery day retracing the bushwhack back down the drainage toward Ross Lake.
sectionBreakdown.fromTo: Rest and begin the hike out

sectionBreakdown.note: Finish the brushy descent back to Ross Lake and catch the water taxi back across the lake to the car.
sectionBreakdown.fromTo: Bushwhack out and boat back to the car
